title: Overlooking the One Thing That Changes Everything
speaker: Aaron Brockett
goal: Challenge each man to identify and surrender an idol that competes with Jesus in his life.
scripture_instructions: Read Mark 10:17-22 aloud, pausing after 22. Then read Mark 10:28-31. Let the initial reactions land before diving into questions.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: What's something trivial you refused to give away as a kid?
icebreakers.note: Helps break the ice with humor and familiarity.

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: Share a time you missed an opportunity by holding on too tight.
icebreakers.note: Encourages sharing life experiences and lessons learned.

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: What's one thing you wouldn't want to give up today?

sections.title: Childlike Reception
sections.setup: Jesus challenges the disciples to embrace childlike faith, emphasizing a posture of receiving rather than achieving. Children epitomize trust and dependence, traits often lost in adulthood as self-sufficiency builds.
sections.say: The disciples missed a key point: the kingdom of God belongs to those who receive it like children.

questions.ask: When did you approach faith with the receptiveness of a child?
questions.lead: Jesus said the kingdom belongs to the childlike.
questions.probe: What let you drop your guard and openly receive?

questions.ask: Where in your life do you insist on achieving rather than receiving?
questions.lead: Receiving implies letting go of control.
questions.probe: What would it cost you to release control in that area?

questions.ask: When have you defaulted to checklists of faith rather than trust?
questions.lead: Childlike faith is marked by trust, not by commandment-keeping.
questions.probe: What does it protect you from confronting in yourself?

questions.ask: Where does the adult world's pressure rob you of simple trust?
questions.lead: The story of the children's blessing highlights contrasts with material worries.
questions.probe: What fear keeps you clinging to complexity over simplicity?

reflection_questions: When have I approached faith with childlike receptiveness?
Where do I insist on achieving rather than receiving?
When have I defaulted to checklists of faith rather than trust?
Where does the adult world's pressure rob me of simple trust?

sections.title: Encountering the Rich Young Ruler
sections.setup: The rich young ruler sought eternal life, confident in his moral achievements. But Jesus knew his heart, pressing him on possessions being a stumbling block to real discipleship. We see our struggle: sincere intentions divided by deeper idols.
sections.say: Jesus' conversation with the rich young ruler uncovers what's below his good intentions.

questions.ask: What's the one possession or value you won't release for Jesus?
questions.lead: The ruler wanted eternal life without letting go.
questions.probe: What deeper fear or identity depends on it?

questions.ask: Who tells you the hard truths out of love today?
questions.lead: Jesus loved the young man but asked hard things.
questions.probe: What are you avoiding by ignoring their counsel?

questions.ask: When did a pursuit of security leave you unsatisfied?
questions.lead: The man's sorrow marked deep attachment to wealth.
questions.probe: What does that pattern continue to cost you in relationships or faith?

questions.ask: How have you responded when a pursuit fell short of offering fulfillment?
questions.lead: The rich young ruler walked away sad, unable to part with his wealth.
questions.probe: What did it expose about your priorities or fears?

reflection_questions: What's the one possession or value I won't release for Jesus?
Who tells me the hard truths out of love today?
When did a pursuit of security leave me unsatisfied?
How have I responded when a pursuit fell short of offering fulfillment?

sections.title: True Discipleship
sections.setup: True discipleship challenges us to recognize and let go of idols, anything overvalued above God. Jesus, our ultimate example, gave all for us. Identifying idols demands honest reflection on what competes for our hearts.
sections.say: Jesus doesn't want your money; He wants your heart surrendered to Him.

questions.ask: How do you secure your sense of self-worth outside of God?
questions.lead: Jesus challenged rich man's perceived self-sufficiency.
questions.probe: Where do you turn when those things fail you?

questions.ask: What belief about church or faith subtly competes with reliance on Jesus?
questions.lead: The disciples sought clarity on salvation beyond wealth.
questions.probe: When did it subtly limit your spiritual growth or outreach?

questions.ask: What's one comfort you hold back from surrendering to Jesus?
questions.lead: Jesus removed the ruler's escape route to reliance on wealth.
questions.probe: How does keeping it preserve an illusion of control?

questions.ask: Where can embracing sacrificial generosity reshape your view of security?
questions.lead: Jesus made eternal wealth available through His poverty and sacrifice.
questions.probe: Where will retraining trust in God's provision first test your comfort?

reflection_questions: How do I secure my sense of self-worth outside of God?
What belief about church or faith subtly competes with reliance on Jesus?
What's one comfort I hold back from surrendering to Jesus?
Where can embracing sacrificial generosity reshape my view of security?

closing_go_around: Name the hardest thing you could let go of but want to this week. How will you start?
prayer: Pray for courage to release idols, to embrace trust like a child this week, and for any hidden fear to be replaced with God's provision.

cheat_sheet.response: Gently redirect back to his initial response or story.
Validate their feelings, and remind them Jesus didn’t ask for the man’s money per se, it's about heart gestured trust.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: A participant stays silent in group repeatedly.
cheat_sheet.response: Pair up: invite him for a one-on-one check-in post-group to see if something's blocking sharing.
Reframe: ask how seeing something as a child would change a real-life approach today.
Ask him to think of a specific life example or decision impacted by topic.
Guide to wider focus on where trust lies: wealth isn’t the only idol.

key_themes: True security is in Jesus, not possessions.
Kingdom invitation comes with personal surrender.
Idols creep in unnoticed through good things.
Receiving over achievement defines real faith.
Jesus exposed identity sources deeper than religious checklist.
commitment_prompt: Identify and release one thing to Jesus' control this week and come prepared to discuss next time.
thesis: Jesus is the rich ruler who gave up everything; will we surrender what holds us back from Him?
outline: Conversation with rich young ruler reveals heart issue
sensitivities: Discussing personal idols may bring up vulnerability or past hurts.
Financial security concerns could be tender for those with history of loss.
obstacle: What idol or fear holds you tight when you think of surrendering completely to Jesus this week?
carry: By next week, ask how the week's surrender attempt went, and what God revealed through it.
